extension.description: A Kodi metadata scraper for movies, backed by your self-hosted Chronicle server. Unlike a normal scraper, it never talks to TMDB or any other upstream source directly -- it only ever asks Chronicle, which resolves-and-creates the item through whichever metadata providers you've already configured there, so Kodi always ends up seeing exactly what Chronicle itself would show for that title -- movie sets, multi-source ratings, trailers and all. Distinct from Chronicle_Scrobbler (which reports watch progress) -- this addon supplies library metadata during "Change Content" / library scans. TV shows are a separate sibling addon, script.chronicle.scraper.tv -- install both if you track both; see that addon's own description for why they can't be one addon.
extension.news:
v3.17.13 - Fixes v3.17.12 creating empty duplicate shows. A show is now looked up by its own TMDB/IMDb/TVDB ids first; the title+year search (which CREATES a new show when the year Kodi reports is wrong -- Kodi's year for A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms was Star Trek: Discovery's) is only the last resort. Also corrects a show's year. This is what actually repairs A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, Alien: Earth, Big Brother, Battle on the Beach and Chad Powers. v3.17.12 - IMPORTANT fix. The periodic sync trusted a saved Kodi-id -> Chronicle-id map that goes wrong whenever Kodi renumbers its library, so some items were matched to a different title entirely (e.g. "A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms" to "Star Trek: Discovery") and had that item's ratings, watched marks and -- since v3.17.9 -- episode titles and plots written onto them. Every match is now checked against the title before anything is written; a mismatch is re-resolved, and skipped if it still disagrees. Install this before the next sync runs. v3.17.11 - A movie file is now matched to Chronicle by the year in its own file name instead of Kodi's own year (which is wrong whenever a scrape picked the wrong film, e.g. "Total Recall (2012).mkv" scraped as the 1990 film) -- so its watched state, rating and details stop being cross-linked to another film. The post-scan check also corrects a movie's cast, studio and country when they differ, not only its title/plot/genre. v3.17.10 - Replaces v3.17.9's episode matching, which would have renumbered the second half of multi-episode files. An episode is now matched to Chronicle by what its FILE is: the title in the file name when it identifies exactly one Chronicle episode of that season, otherwise the numbers (Kodi's own for a multi-episode file). Fixes files whose numbering differs from Chronicle's list getting another episode's title, plot, thumb, rating and watched status. Kodi's season/episode numbers are never rewritten. v3.17.9 - Episodes now match Chronicle by the season/episode in the FILE NAME instead of Kodi's own numbers (which are wrong whenever a scrape mis-numbered an episode, pairing the file with a different episode's title, plot, thumb, rating and watched status), and a wrong season/episode number in Kodi is corrected. The periodic sync also now compares every episode's title, plot, aired date and thumb, not only ratings and watched state. v3.17.8 - The periodic sync now also corrects a TV show's own text (plot, premiered, rating, genre, studio) when it differs from Chronicle, the same as movies and episodes already were. Only differing fields are written; nothing is blanked. v3.17.7 - Reset comparison now converts the server's UTC reset time to the device's local time, and a reset no longer sends an empty last-played value. v3.17.6 - Watched marks reset in Chronicle now stick. Resetting a movie, episode, season or show in Chronicle records a reset time; a Kodi device whose own watch predates it clears its playcount on the next sync instead of re-importing it. v3.17.5 - Fixes v3.17.4's own full sync-check never actually correcting a wrong poster: it pushed art through VideoLibrary.SetMovieDetails' own art parameter, but Kodi always uses a movie's local "-poster.jpg" file when one exists, ignoring that parameter entirely -- the same reason the normal scrape path never trusted it either. Confirmed live: the Ghostbusters (2016) fix landed for every other field, but the poster kept showing the wrong (1984) image regardless. Now calls the same sync_movie_art() mechanism the normal scrape uses (rewrites the local file, invalidates Kodi's texture cache) for every resolved movie, unconditionally -- its own skip-cache keeps an already-correct poster cheap.
v3.17.4 - New: after every video library scan finishes (Kodi's own startup scan, your own manual "Update Library", or this addon's own new-content detection), checks every movie Kodi already has against Chronicle's current data -- matched by the exact video file, never by title/year -- and corrects only whatever actually disagrees. Fixes movies that were scraped with the wrong data at some point and never corrected since (root-caused live: a "Ghostbusters (2016)" file carrying the 1984 film's title/year/plot). New settings toggle "Verify every movie matches Chronicle after each scan" under New Content Detection, on by default.
v3.17.3 - Fixed art not actually updating in Kodi after Chronicle's pick changed: sync_movie_art() overwrote a movie's local poster/fanart file on disk correctly, but never told Kodi to drop its own cached copy of that same path. Kodi's texture cache only re-hashes a local file about once a day, so the new art sat correct on disk while Kodi kept showing the old cached picture until that check happened to come round. Now invalidates the cached texture immediately after every overwrite, the same fix collection_sync.py already used for movie-set art.
v3.17.2 - Fixed: a movie's own local "-thumb.jpg" file (a legacy filename some libraries still carry from before this addon existed) was never kept in sync with Chronicle's own poster pick -- only "-poster.jpg"/"-fanart.jpg" were. Kodi's generic "thumbnail" field (what list/grid views actually show by default, separate from the "poster" art type) can resolve to that legacy file when present, so a freshly-corrected poster could still never actually display anywhere Kodi shows "thumbnail" instead of "poster" specifically. "-thumb.jpg" is now kept in sync with the same poster candidate.
v3.17.1 - Correction to v3.17.0's own metadata-refresh feature, shipped and then reworked the same day: that version checked Chronicle for changed items on a periodic timer (every 15 minutes by default), with its own "Metadata Refresh" settings toggle. Per-user direction, this is now tied entirely to Kodi's existing native "Update library on startup" checkbox instead -- no new setting to configure. It runs at most once per Kodi session, only when that checkbox is on, and only as the very last step after the startup library scan it triggers (or defers to a sibling Chronicle Scraper addon for) actually finishes -- never racing or overlapping the scan itself, never a recurring background poll. The "Metadata Refresh" settings category from v3.17.0 has been removed.
v3.17.0 - New: this addon now pushes a real refresh to Kodi whenever an already-scraped movie's data changes in Chronicle (re-enrichment, an admin edit, a pinned image), instead of that item sitting stale until someone manually clicks "Refresh information" on it. Confirmed live (2026-09-19): a movie/show's own local Kodi entry doesn't automatically switch to a newly-pinned poster just because a later getdetails() call lists it as the new top candidate -- Kodi keeps whatever it originally chose until something forces a real VideoLibrary.Refresh. This addon polls Chronicle for its own already-known items that have changed since it last scraped them and fires that refresh itself -- never a full library scan, only the specific items that actually changed (see v3.17.1 above for how this is actually triggered).
v3.16.6 - Confirmed live (2026-09-18) the single largest remaining per-movie cost, after the scan-speed fixes below: sync_movie_art unconditionally re-downloaded poster+fanart from their remote CDN URLs on every single movie, every single scan, even when nothing had changed since the last successful sync -- a real network image fetch (up to 20s timeout) instead of a fast local check. Now skips the download when the exact same URL was already written last time AND the local file's own size still matches what was written then (size, not mere existence, so Kodi silently reverting the file's content -- the documented reason this always overwrote unconditionally in the first place -- is still caught and corrected). Also adds permanent per-step timing to every getdetails() call (Chronicle API, folder lookup, collection art, rating/resume sync, movie art) so any future slowdown shows up directly in kodi.log instead of requiring another investigation from scratch.
v3.16.5 - Fixes a very slow full-library scan (reported live 2026-09-18, roughly one movie every 30-40s regardless of how fast Chronicle's own API responded -- see Chronicle's own v0.20.22 for that separate, already-fixed half of it). Root cause: during an active scan, VideoLibrary predictably doesn't have the movie currently being scraped yet (Kodi hasn't committed it), so this addon's own source-browsing fallback (find_movie_location) runs on nearly every single movie -- and it re-lists every configured video source from scratch over the network each time, even though that listing is essentially identical from one movie to the next, seconds apart. Now caches each source's listing for 60 seconds, so a full scan lists each source about once a minute instead of once per movie.
v3.16.4 - New: this addon's own background service now reproduces what a manual "Scan Library" does once Kodi's native "Update library on startup" checkbox finishes its own too-early pass -- confirmed live that checkbox fires a real scan before network shares are mounted, so it sees an empty/unreachable source and finishes in under a minute instead of the real many-thousand-file scan a later manual call does. Per-user direction: fixed WITHOUT touching that checkbox -- it stays the only control, nothing new to configure. This addon's service now independently reads that same setting and, only if it's on, waits (bounded) for this addon's own source folder to actually be reachable, then fires one full scan itself, matching manual-scan semantics. Code-review fixes applied before release: doesn't fire a second overlapping scan while one's already running, doesn't fire twice on a device with both this and the TV addon installed, and the reachability check itself can no longer hang forever on an unresponsive share.
v3.16.3 - REVERTED v3.16.1's datetime.strptime() priming fix: on this device it failed EVERY time at module-import time instead of fixing the rare original race, taking the ENTIRE background service down on every single Kodi startup (no watch/rating sync, no collection art sync, no scan signal at all). The original bug (one rare, tolerable failure during a huge concurrent burst) is far preferable to that. See lib/progress_sync.py's own note -- needs a real on-device repro before trying again, not a textbook fix applied blind.
v3.16.2 - Fixed a real, actively-firing bug in lib/collection_sync.py's stale-set-art repair (pre-existing, unrelated to the NFO removal below): clearing a dead art reference sent an empty string to Kodi's VideoLibrary.SetMovieSetDetails, which that API rejects outright for ANY art slot -- since art is one combined object per call, that single bad value silently dropped every other art update batched with it, for any collection that had even one dead reference to clear. Confirmed live: this was firing for dozens of collections on one device. Fixed by sending null instead of ''.
v3.16.1 - Fixed a pre-existing, unrelated bug found live during a heavy rescan session (2026-09-13): lib/progress_sync.py's datetime.strptime() call could occasionally fail ("'NoneType' object is not callable") when Kodi's worker-thread pool raced its very first call in the process -- a well-known CPython lazy-import hazard, fixed by priming it once at module load. Also removed a few more pieces of now-dead code left over from the NFO removal below (unused chronicle_client._get_bytes(), unused legacy_nfo.py stash functions in the TV addon).
v3.16.0 - Removed local NFO writing/rebuilding entirely (write_nfo, write_streamdetails, "Rebuild local NFOs from Chronicle", "Automatically rebuild NFOs after every library scan", and the corner-status rebuild widget) -- per-user direction (2026-09-13) after it was suspected of interfering with TV show scanning reliability during a heavy rescan session. Chronicle's own API is the source of truth this scraper reads from directly; no local NFO was ever required for it to work. If you relied on a local NFO for another tool, that data is no longer written or refreshed by this addon.
v3.15.5 - No functional change to this addon -- paired version bump alongside TV v1.11.7's removal of per-episode NFO writing, whose shared pipeline (nfo_rebuild.py, in this addon's own lib/) picked up a documentation-only note explaining why its own "episode" kind branch is now permanently unreachable rather than removed. See the TV addon's own changelog for the actual fix.
v3.15.4 - Movie collections now belong entirely to this addon (per-user decision, 2026-09-12): a new periodic "Collection Art" task (Settings -> Collection Art, on by default) refreshes every collection's art in Kodi's own "Movie set information folder" from Chronicle, via a new server endpoint (movies/collections) -- not just the collections that happen to get touched as a side effect of one of their member movies being rescraped. Replaces Chronicle_Scrobbler's own retired collection-art sync, which pushed the same art a different way (directly via Kodi's API instead of into this dedicated folder). Subject to the same never-run-during-an-active-scan control as the existing Watch History and Ratings sync (and Chronicle's own server-side NFO generation) -- see that task's own settings help text.
v3.15.3 - Root-caused live (2026-09-12): during an active library scan, Chronicle's own scheduled NFO-generation sweep and this addon's live per-item pushes were independently rebuilding and writing the same freshly-scanned item's NFO within seconds of each other -- pure waste that competed with the scan itself for the same server/IO capacity, slowing the whole scan down (confirmed live: 6 episodes of a single show taking far longer than they should have). service.py now sends Chronicle a short heartbeat (via the existing corner-status idle loop, already polling Kodi's own scan state and this addon's scraper-activity tail every ~3s) while a scan is active, so the server-side sweep pauses itself for the duration instead of contending with it. No settings change needed -- this is on for everyone automatically.
v3.15.2 - lib/tvshow_location.py's find_show_location() now caches a show's resolved (folder, tvshowid) for 15 minutes instead of re-resolving it via Kodi's own API on every single call -- fixes a real household TV library that never fully scanned in on the sibling TV addon (same root cause, same fix, this addon's own copy of the file per its own "fix it in both copies" doc -- nfo_rebuild.py here uses the identical function for its own TV rebuild-queue items). See the TV addon's own v1.11.3 changelog entry for the full root-cause explanation.
v3.15.1 - Two corrections to v3.15.0's new-content scan-signal feature, both found during review before it ever shipped in a release build:
(1) The triggered scan now only ever touches the source folder(s) THIS addon is actually configured as the scraper for on this device (read live from Kodi's own video database -- never cached, and never inferred from Chronicle's own server-side folder paths, since a device's local source naming has no reliable relationship to those). Previously it called VideoLibrary.Scan with no directory at all, which scans every configured source regardless of content type -- on a device where this addon is set up for TV only, that meant a TV-triggered scan was also touching movie folders this addon has no relationship with at all.
(2) The periodic check is now OFF by default (was: always checked every 3 minutes). Reason: a triggered VideoLibrary.Scan fires Kodi's global onScanFinished event, which every other addon's own Monitor reacts to independently -- confirmed live that this cascades into Chronicle_Scrobbler's own VideoLibrary.Clean and SIMKL Scrobbler's own full sync pass, not just this addon's work. This device still always checks once when Kodi starts (catches anything imported overnight with zero configuration), and a new "Periodically check for new content" setting lets you opt back into recurring checks at an interval you choose (default 120 minutes, was effectively 3).
v3.15.0 - New: this addon now polls Chronicle every few minutes for "new movie/TV content was imported" and, if due, triggers its own local library scan (VideoLibrary.Scan) to pick it up -- closes a real gap where a brand-new file (confirmed live on three shows) never got discovered at all until someone noticed and clicked "Update Library" by hand, since VideoLibrary.Refresh* (what every other sync in this addon uses) only works on an item Kodi already has a library entry for. Pull, not push: this device polls and scans itself via its own local xbmc.executeJSONRPC -- Chronicle's server never calls out to any device for this, so nothing here needs "Allow remote control via HTTP" turned on.
v3.14.1 - Per-user report (2026-09-09): an item marked watched still showed a progress percentage in Kodi. Root cause: a device with its own stale local resume point (partial playback that was never finished ON THAT DEVICE) never had it cleared -- Chronicle's own resume position clears the moment an item is marked watched, so the reconciliation logic correctly decided there was nothing new to push for resume, but that left the device's existing local resume point completely untouched even as the SAME reconciliation pass set playcount=1 for the watched status. Both the inline per-scrape sync and the periodic watch_rating_sync background pass now explicitly zero the resume point whenever they mark an item watched, so a device never shows "watched" and "partway through" at the same time again.
v3.14.0 - Per-user report (2026-09-08): a device whose local library covers only a fraction of the shared catalog was claiming, failing to resolve, and releasing tens of thousands of items of the same doomed kind (movie/show/episode) in a single rebuild run -- confirmed live, 20,722 of 20,875 items in one run, almost entirely episodes this device genuinely doesn't hold locally. The rebuild now tracks a per-kind consecutive-failure streak; once a kind fails 10 times in a row, it's excluded from further claims for the rest of that run (both server-side, so Chronicle stops handing that kind out, and locally, so an already-claimed item of that kind is released immediately without attempting a lookup already known to fail). Resets fresh on every run, so it self-heals the moment this device's own library coverage improves.
v3.13.0 - Per-user request (2026-09-06), after confirming a single device was carrying a 26,000+ item rebuild backlog alone with no other Kodi instance running concurrently: the rebuild queue now processes up to 3 items at once instead of strictly one at a time, meaningfully speeding up a large backlog. Live-validated against a real 26,000+ item queue after the change: healthy 9-18s per-item completion times, no regression toward the Kodi-refresh-pipeline-backup issue v2.9.0 fixed. Also fixes two real bugs found and verified during code review of this change: two items from the same Chronicle collection (or two episodes sharing a generic filename) processed in the same moment could race writing the same shared local file (collection art / a legacy-NFO stash), and cancelling a rebuild could now take up to a full item timeout to actually stop instead of the near-immediate stop the single-item design always guaranteed -- both fixed. An unexpected error processing one item no longer silently kills that item's worker thread with nothing in kodi.log to show it.
v3.12.0 - New: automatic watch-history and rating sync. Previously, rating/resume/ watched-status changes made directly in Kodi only ever reached Chronicle (and vice versa) as a side effect of Kodi re-scraping an item -- which, per v3.11.0's own fix, now only happens for genuinely new items or during an explicit rebuild pass. Added a separate, lightweight, non-destructive sync (new "Watch History and Ratings" settings category) that reconciles this directly via Kodi's own VideoLibrary fields, with no local file writes at all: on by default, runs once shortly after this service starts (toggle), and on a recurring interval you can set in 30-minute steps (default every 2 hours). A "Sync Watch History and Ratings Now" button runs it on demand any time. Caches each item's resolved Chronicle id locally after its first successful sync, so repeat passes skip Chronicle's slower resolve-or-create lookup entirely for already-known items.
v3.11.1 - Fixed a gap in v3.11.0 below: a settings.xml default="..." only ever applies to a value Kodi has never persisted, so simply changing write_nfo/auto_rebuild_on_scan's shipped default did nothing for an already-installed copy of this addon (both settings would have stayed off forever, no matter how the addon was updated). Added a one-time code migration (lib/settings_upgrade.py) that actually turns both on for an existing install the moment any part of this addon next runs -- no Kodi restart, and no manual settings change needed.
v3.11.0 - Root-caused why episodes/rating/progress changes were failing to reach Kodi at all on some libraries: both "Recreate local NFO file from Chronicle's data" and "Automatically rebuild NFOs after every library scan" defaulted OFF, so the one mechanism that gets Kodi to re-ask this scraper about an already-scraped item (a rebuild-forced refresh) never ran -- not just for NFOs, but for the rating/resume/watched reconciliation that also only happens inside that same callback. Both settings now default ON. The automatic rebuild pass also now shows a progress bar and start/completion notifications, matching the manual "Rebuild local NFOs" action -- previously it ran completely silently, log-only. Added a safety check: if auto-rebuild is on but NFO-writing somehow gets turned off, it now refuses (with a warning notification) instead of silently deleting local NFOs it will never rewrite. HTTP calls to Chronicle now retry twice with a short backoff on a transient network failure, absorbing the kind of timeout a full-library rescan's request burst can cause. Chronicle's own rating/watch endpoints (web UI and the rating add-on) now push a live refresh to Kodi immediately after a rating change or a completed watch, instead of only in the next rebuild pass.
v3.10.0 - Per-user request: speed up getting a Chronicle metadata change out to Kodi. Editing an item in Chronicle now writes its NFO straight to disk immediately (server-side, via the same sidecar builder v3.9.0 introduced) and pushes a targeted refresh to any Kodi instance that has already reported its own internal id for that item -- instead of waiting for a manual/scheduled "Recreate local NFO" pass or that device's own next library scan. This addon now self-registers its own remote-control address with Chronicle (once after "Connect to Chronicle" succeeds, and periodically thereafter) so the server has somewhere to push to; skipped silently if Kodi's own "Allow remote control via HTTP" (Settings -> Services -> Control) is off, which remains a fully supported configuration for every other feature this addon has. Also now reports this device's own Kodi movieid back to Chronicle on every ordinary scan, which is what makes the targeted push possible without waiting for a rebuild.
v3.9.0 - "Recreate local NFO" now fetches the NFO's own document pre-built from Chronicle's server (a new companion plugin, Chronicle.Plugin.Kodi.NFO) instead of building the XML on this device in Python -- same document, same fields, just assembled on the more capable machine. This addon now only splices in the two things Chronicle's server structurally cannot know: Kodi's own streamdetails probe and local art files already sitting on disk. No behaviour change for ordinary library scans (NFO writing was, and remains, rebuild-pass-only) -- this only affects how the "Recreate local NFO" action itself builds each document.
v3.8.0 - Per-user request (2026-09-05): a movie completed on one Shield stayed permanently unwatched on another, with no error -- nothing was actually broken, the existing resume-position reconciliation was simply never able to help here. Chronicle clears its own resume-percent/timestamp the moment an item is marked watched (nothing left to "resume"), so a fully-completed item carried no signal at all for the scraper to compare against another Kodi instance's own state. Watched status is now reconciled the same way resume position already was, but from its own signal (Chronicle's watched flag and completion time, which are never cleared) -- whichever side is more recent pushes its playcount/lastplayed to the other, in either direction.
v3.7.0 - Per-user request (2026-09-04): the movie-sets folder popup ("Movie collections folder not reachable: smb://...") fired on the very first failed attempt to create/write that folder, with no retry -- a momentary SMB/NAS hiccup (share still waking up, a brief network blip) looked identical to the folder genuinely being gone. Both the folder-creation check and the per-set artwork write now retry up to 5 times, 10 seconds apart, matching how Kodi's own library scanner treats any other folder it can't immediately reach. The popup still fires (it remains something the user can act on -- fix the share/path in Kodi's settings) but only once every retry has actually been exhausted.
v3.6.0 - Per-user redirect (2026-08-30): "I don't want a separate sync task in Kodi for ratings. this needs to happen with the scraper automatically as part of the scrape process. Kodi may not call the scraper for each video, but you will still need to synchronize the playback progress and the ratings for each video at some point in the scrape process." Replaces Chronicle_Scrobbler's every-30-minutes background rating/resume sync (removed there, see its own changelog) with reconciliation folded directly into every getdetails call this addon already makes -- no separate task, no extra JSON-RPC write. Rating always pushes Chronicle -> Kodi (via InfoTagVideo.setUserRating() on the same ListItem Kodi is already consuming this scrape -- Kodi has no per-rating timestamp to compare against, so there's no safe way to detect a fresher local value). Resume position is genuinely bidirectional: Kodi's own lastplayed/resume/playcount is looked up once per scrape and compared against Chronicle's ResumeUpdatedAt, same "most recent wins" rule as before -- Chronicle ahead sets Kodi's resume point via InfoTagVideo.setResumePoint() (still inline, no extra write); Kodi ahead reports its position into Chronicle via the existing scrobble endpoint (server-side already guards against a stale value winning). Applies on every scrape this addon runs -- a new file's first scan, a manual "Refresh information," or an NFO rebuild pass -- not on Kodi's own unprompted incremental scans (which skip an item that already has a local NFO), same as every other field this addon supplies. v3.5.5 - Writes each actor's Chronicle-resolved headshot into the NFO's <actor><thumb> tag when Chronicle has one (Phase 6 of the People feature, docs/plans/2026-08-28-people-section-design.md) -- Kodi's own actor NFO schema already supports this, it just never had anything to put there before. No visible change until enough people have been resolved with real photos server-side. v3.5.4 - Per-user correction (2026-08-29): "you delete everything first and then rewrite everything ... look at each video item individually and delete and rebuild rather than doing all the deletes and then the whole rebuild." "Rebuild local NFOs from Chronicle" now fully processes one item (delete its old NFO, refresh, wait for the new one to actually reappear) before moving to the next, instead of deleting every item's NFO in a fast burst and only THEN waiting on the whole batch draining -- the old order meant the entire library could sit with no valid local NFO at all for the whole multi-minute wait, a real data-loss risk if the run was ever interrupted partway through. At most one item is ever without a valid NFO now, for at most 60s. Runs fully in the background with no Cancel control once started (per-user decision) -- same tradeoff the old wait phase already had for most of a run's duration, just now for the whole thing. v3.5.3 - Per-user correction (2026-08-29): "I only ever want them to open the regular settings window, not whatever [the old action-list menu] is" -- launching this addon from Kodi's Add-on browser now goes straight to Settings instead of showing a Dialog().select() menu first. Test Connection, previously only reachable from that menu, now has its own action button in Settings' Connection category (Edit Connection/Change Chronicle URL/Rebuild local NFOs already had theirs). v3.5.2 - Fixes invalid XML in resources/settings.xml (a "--" inside an actual XML comment, not just element text) caught by a repo-wide sweep after this same mistake showed up several times tonight in other files. No functional/behavior change; a full sweep of every .xml/.csproj/.props/.targets file under this whole project tree confirms nothing else is affected. v3.5.1 - Per-user request (2026-08-29): "each of the add-ons could check each other for the chronicle URL and just copy it in from another working add-on... save the typing." "Edit Connection"'s URL prompt now checks the other installed Chronicle addons (Scraper TV, Scrobbler) for an already-configured chronicle_url and pre-fills the entry dialog with the first one found, instead of always starting blank -- still one explicit confirm step, never silently auto-connects. A sibling that isn't installed, or has nothing set yet itself, is simply skipped. v3.5.0 - New: the main menu now shows connection status (and WHO's connected -- "Connected as {name}", via GET /users/me) directly in the menu heading, before you'd ever click "Edit Connection" -- per-user request (2026-08-28): "update the scrapers and the scrobbler to show that they're connected or not before they try to make a connection... say who was connected also." 5s-bounded so an unreachable server doesn't make the menu itself feel stuck; falls back to the last-known name (cached in a new hidden connected_display_name setting) rather than regressing to a bare "Connected" on a transient network blip. v3.4.0 - TV episode NFOs still never got written during a rebuild even after v3.3.0's write_nfo-mirroring fix landed: confirmed live via kodi.log (2026-08-28) that tv_addon's lib/tvshow_location.py get_episode() -- which asks VideoLibrary.GetEpisodes(tvshowid) for an episode's own file path -- came back empty for essentially every episode processed during a rebuild, not because the file was missing (nfo_rebuild.py's own earlier, pre-refresh full-library GetEpisodes call found a real path for every one of them) but because VideoLibrary.RefreshEpisode()'s own in-flight scrape tears down that exact episode's library row until the scrape's own getepisodedetails() callback returns -- the episode was asking VideoLibrary about itself, from inside itself, before it was done. New lib/episode_path_cache.py (duplicated into tv_addon/lib/, same special://temp/ cross-addon pattern as legacy_nfo.py/rebuild_state.py) stashes each episode's already-known-good file path right before nfo_rebuild.py issues its refresh; get_episode_details() now falls back to that stash whenever the live VideoLibrary lookup comes back empty. If both come up empty (shouldn't happen in practice now), that episode's NFO write is skipped with a clear kodi.log warning instead of the previous silent no-op. v3.3.0 - New: changing "Recreate local NFO file from Chronicle's data" or "Include technical file info" (via Settings, or the auto-enable prompt in "Rebuild local NFOs from Chronicle") now offers to apply the identical change to the sibling script.chronicle.scraper.tv addon too, if installed. Root cause of a live 2026-08-28 report ("NFO rebuild stuck at the same count for over an hour"): the two addons keep entirely separate settings.xml files, and TV's write_nfo had silently drifted to off while the movie side's stayed on -- an in-progress rebuild kept successfully re-scraping every TV episode with nothing ever actually writing to disk, and nothing in kodi.log said why. New lib/settings_mirror.py (duplicated into tv_addon/lib/ for the same reason nfo_rebuild.py's other helpers are); asks once per change, covering both settings together, and only when the sibling addon is actually installed. v3.2.3 - Code-review fixes to the Connect flow: a QR pairing that was approved on the phone but whose one-time key never reached this device (e.g. a poll that timed out client-side even though the request actually completed) used to leave the QR window stuck open forever -- it now shows a clear error and asks you to try Connect again. The Settings status field could briefly flash back to "Not connected" immediately after a successful connect -- fixed. Declining the loopback-URL warning now actually cancels the connect instead of proceeding against that URL anyway. New "Change Chronicle URL" action (main menu and Settings) is the first way to correct a wrong URL once one is saved -- there was previously no way to do this short of editing settings.xml by hand. A malformed response from Chronicle during device-auth now shows a specific error instead of crashing to a generic "Connect failed unexpectedly". v3.2.2 - v3.2.1 fixed _initiate()'s own cross-instance chronicle_url read but missed an identical one in _poll_loop() -- confirmed live: after approving the device on the phone, the QR window never closed, with "Poll error: unknown url type: '/api/v1/auth/device/{code}/poll'" in the log -- a schemeless, hostless URL, meaning _poll_loop()'s own independent ADDON.getSetting('chronicle_url') read came back empty even though _initiate()'s POST (already fixed to use self._base_url) had worked moments earlier and produced a real QR code. _poll_loop() now also uses self._base_url. v3.2.1 - Root cause of v3.2.0's URL-entry-still-not-working reports found via logging: confirmed live that default.py's own ADDON.setSetting('chronicle_url', ...) is not reliably visible to device_auth.py's SEPARATE xbmcaddon.Addon() instance's very next getSetting('chronicle_url') call -- same process, same addon, same settings.xml, one line apart, and still empty. Kodi's Addon() binding apparently doesn't guarantee cross-instance read-your-own-write consistency. DeviceAuthManager now takes the resolved URL as a constructor parameter instead of re-reading it independently -- default.py hands over the value it just resolved (or prompted for and saved) directly, sidestepping the cross-instance question entirely rather than continuing to chase it through Kodi's settings storage. v3.2.0 - BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, per user request: the Chronicle URL now has exactly ONE entry point instead of two. Settings' own chronicle_url field is now read-only (enable="false") -- it was never reliably editable there to begin with (v3.1.6/v3.1.8's own investigation confirmed Kodi's on-screen-keyboard edit to that field doesn't always land in the saved value, even after the whole Settings dialog closes). "Connect to Chronicle" is renamed "Edit Connection" and is now the only place a URL is ever entered: it prompts via a proven-reliable dialog ONLY when there isn't already a saved URL, so an already-connected reconnect skips straight to the QR window with no prompt -- a working URL is never typed twice. Also removed: the auto-bounce to Settings on first run (no longer needed, since "Edit Connection" is directly reachable from the main menu and handles an empty URL itself), and all of v3.1.6-3.1.8's Action(Back)/reopen-Settings/settle-wait/fallback-prompt machinery in default.py and device_auth.py -- none of it is necessary anymore now that Settings' text field is out of the picture entirely. v3.1.8 - Two fixes from a confirmed live report: closing Settings (v3.1.6) did NOT fix it after all -- chronicle_url still read empty even after the dialog was fully closed, not just delayed, meaning the on-screen-keyboard edit to that field isn't reliably landing in the underlying setting at all on some setups. _initiate() now falls back to a single guaranteed-reliable xbmcgui.Dialog().input() prompt when chronicle_url is still empty after everything else has been tried, saves it explicitly, and proceeds -- only appears when the Settings-based path has actually failed, never adding friction to a working connect. Also: the "Status" field in Settings was showing "Connected" purely because an api_key from a past successful connection was still saved, even while chronicle_url was empty and every current Connect attempt was failing outright -- _refresh_auth_status() now requires both, matching _is_configured()'s own check. v3.1.7 - Settings now reopens automatically right after v3.1.6's Action(Back) close (Addon.OpenSettings, non-blocking, unlike ADDON.openSettings()), so the forced close reads as a quick visual blip instead of dumping you back at whatever was behind Settings for the rest of the Connect flow -- Kodi's own window manager should restore focus to wherever you left off (e.g. "Connect to Chronicle" itself) automatically. The QR window then appears on top of that reopened Settings screen. v3.1.6 - Root cause finally confirmed by reading settings.xml directly moments after a failed Connect attempt: chronicle_url was still at its empty default over a minute after the user typed a URL and could see it sitting in the field -- not a timing race (v3.1.5's settle-wait didn't help, because there was nothing to wait FOR), an ORDERING one. Kodi's addon Settings dialog only writes settings.xml to disk when the whole dialog closes, not per-field as focus moves between controls, and "Connect to Chronicle" is a button INSIDE that same still-open dialog. _connect_to_chronicle() now closes Settings first (Action(Back), only when Window.IsActive(addonsettings) confirms it's actually open -- a no-op from the main-menu path, never risking closing the wrong window) before reading chronicle_url and connecting. v3.1.5 - Fixes the actual bug behind v3.1.1's (reverted) URL-confirm prompt, without bringing back the prompt. Confirmed live with v3.1.3/v3.1.4's own logging: chronicle_url read back completely empty immediately after typing a URL and clicking "Connect to Chronicle" from inside the still-open Settings dialog, for a URL that WAS saved correctly moments later -- Kodi's Settings dialog does not always flush a just-edited field to settings.xml synchronously with an action button fired from that same dialog. _initiate() now waits 500ms (imperceptible alongside the real network round-trip that follows) before its first read of chronicle_url, giving Kodi's flush time to land -- fixes both a first-time URL entry and switching to a different URL, with no added dialog or retyping. v3.1.4 - BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: reverts v3.1.1's "confirm the URL before connecting" prompt. The new v3.1.3 logging caught it live: the prompt added a mandatory on-screen-keyboard URL retype to every single Connect attempt, and the actual bug report that led to this revert was the user backing out of that unexpected prompt within ~2 seconds -- not a stale URL ever being used. "Connect to Chronicle" now goes straight to the QR window again, same as before v3.1.1. If a URL edited in Settings and immediately connected-to via the in-Settings action button still ever reads stale, close Settings fully first and click Connect from the main menu instead -- that path always reads the already-flushed value. Diagnostic logging (step-by-step trace, distinct per-addon log prefix) from v3.1.3 stays in place. v3.1.3 - Diagnostic logging only, no behavior change: the Connect flow (default.py's _connect_to_chronicle) now logs every step -- the URL read from disk, what the URL prompt returned, whether it changed, and DeviceAuthManager.run()'s own progress through _initiate()/QR-download/QRDialog construction/doModal(), plus a caught-and-logged traceback if anything in that call raises (a RunScript-launched script has no visible crash surface otherwise -- an unhandled exception would look identical to "the connection window just never showed up"). Also: log prefix changed from the shared "[ChronicleScraper]" to "[ChronicleScraperMovie]" -- it was identical to the sibling TV addon's own prefix, making it impossible to tell which addon a given kodi.log line came from when both are installed. Added while investigating a live report of the Connect window not appearing after switching URLs. v3.1.2 - "Rebuild local NFOs from Chronicle" no longer hard-refuses when "Recreate local NFO file from Chronicle's data" (write_nfo) reads off -- same Settings-dialog-commit-timing risk as v3.1.1's Connect fix (this action button lives in the same Local Files Settings screen as that checkbox), so a box just ticked wasn't guaranteed to be flushed to settings.xml before this brand-new RunScript process read it. Now offers to turn write_nfo on and continue right there instead of bailing out, and writes the setting explicitly before proceeding either way -- so the value actually used is never ambiguous. v3.1.1 - "Connect to Chronicle" now confirms the Chronicle URL directly (a text prompt, pre-filled with whatever's currently saved) instead of trusting chronicle_url on disk. Confirmed live: switching URLs in Settings and immediately clicking "Connect to Chronicle" (the action button lives inside that same still-open Settings dialog) built the QR code against the OLD URL -- a just-typed text field's value isn't guaranteed to be flushed to settings.xml before Kodi launches the RunScript action as a brand new process, so the fresh process could read stale data even though the new value was visibly still sitting in the field. This also fixes the fresh-install case: opening the addon for the first time now prompts for the URL right in the Connect flow instead of requiring a value to already be saved before Connect can do anything with it. v3.1.0 - Two reliability fixes to lib/chronicle_client.py and lib/device_auth.py: (1) urlopen(timeout=N) only bounds the socket once it exists -- the DNS lookup (getaddrinfo) that happens before that isn't covered by that timeout on any platform, so a dead/unreachable DNS server or a stale hostname could hang a "timed" call forever, well past whatever timeout= was passed. Every network call now runs through a thread-based watchdog (call_with_timeout()) that gives up after timeout + 5s even if the underlying call never returns, leaving the runaway thread to die on its own. (2) "Connect to Chronicle" now shows the actual reason a connection attempt failed (empty URL, DNS failure, connection refused, timeout, HTTP error and its body, malformed response) instead of the same generic "Could not contact the Chronicle server" for every failure -- confirmed live complaint: the dialog gave identical text regardless of cause, with no way to tell "you haven't entered a URL yet" apart from "the server is actually down." v3.0.2 - Two fixes, both found in code review: (1) lib/legacy_nfo.py's stash directory had been copied into tv_addon/lib/ without the special://temp/ fix already applied to rebuild_state.py and activity_tracker.py for the same reason -- it was still stashing under special://profile/addon_data/{addon_id}/, which is scoped per addon id. Since a legacy NFO's delete always runs from this (movie) addon's process but the re-scrape that consumes the stash can run from either addon depending on item type, a TV show's stashed data was silently unreachable from the TV addon's own process, breaking legacy-NFO harvesting for TV. Now stashes under special://temp/chronicle_scraper/, matching the other two cross-process signal files. (2) "Rebuild local NFOs from Chronicle" now refuses to run (with an explanatory dialog) if "Recreate local NFO file from Chronicle's data" (write_nfo) is off -- previously it would delete every existing local NFO and never write a replacement, since the scraper's own NFO-writing is gated on that same setting, leaving the library with no local NFOs at all. v3.0.1 - The corner status ("N item(s) processed so far") no longer shows while Kodi's own "Scanning library" indicator is still up -- two progress indicators at once was confusing. It's a display-only change: activity is still tracked underneath the whole time, so the moment Kodi's own indicator disappears, the corner status appears immediately showing the real accumulated count, not starting over from zero. Unrelated to NFO writing or the rebuild pass -- this indicator tracks scraper activity (find/getdetails/getepisodedetails/getartwork) regardless of write_nfo or auto_rebuild_on_scan. v3.0.0 - BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: split into two addons. This addon is now movies-only; install the sibling script.chronicle.scraper.tv addon for TV shows. Root cause: Kodi resolves which script to run for a scrape by addon id alone, not by which extension point (movies vs tvshows) triggered the call -- with both declared in one addon.xml, every TV scrape was silently running this movies script instead of the TV one, no error, nothing in kodi.log. TV shows scanning into the library and getting NFOs has never actually worked with this addon since it started supporting TV, regardless of any TV-specific fix -- the TV code path was architecturally unreachable the whole time. lib/rebuild_state.py and lib/activity_tracker.py's cross-process signal files moved from special://profile/addon_data/{addon_id}/... to special://temp/chronicle_scraper/... so the now-separate movie and TV addons can still coordinate (rebuild-in-progress state, corner status activity) despite having different addon ids. v2.13.3 - BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: local NFO writing (movies, TV shows, and episodes alike) now only ever happens as part of an explicit rebuild pass -- the "Rebuild local NFOs from Chronicle" action, or "Automatically rebuild NFOs after every library scan" -- never inline during an ordinary library scan. Previously, "Recreate local NFO file from Chronicle's data" wrote a fresh local NFO the very first time this scraper scraped a brand-new item, interleaved with the same scan pass that was still discovering other new files; that write (plus, for TV, a VideoLibrary lookup to locate the episode's own file) added local-disk I/O to the scan's critical path for a write that has no bearing on whether the item itself gets into Kodi's library. New lib/rebuild_state.py is a cross-process signal nfo_rebuild.py sets for the duration of a rebuild pass; get_details()/get_episode_details() in both scrapers now check it before writing (or even looking up the file location for) a local NFO. If you rely on "Recreate local NFO file from Chronicle's data" and don't have the auto-rebuild-after-scan setting on, new items now need one manual "Rebuild local NFOs from Chronicle" run (or that setting turned on) to get their NFO written -- it's no longer automatic on first scrape. v2.13.2 - TV shows were silently failing to scan into the library: python/tvshow_scraper.py's run() copied the movies scraper's "only call endOfDirectory() when getdetails() failed" pattern, but the real bundled TV scraper (metadata.tvshows.themoviedb.org.python, ground-truthed against Team Kodi's own source) calls xbmcplugin.endOfDirectory() unconditionally after every action, even a successful getdetails/getepisodedetails/getartwork that already called setResolvedUrl() -- the movies and TV scraper contracts genuinely differ here. Without it, Kodi's plugin handle was never told the TV directory call had finished on success, silently stalling the scan with nothing in kodi.log. Fixed; no behaviour change for movies. (Episode NFOs for brand-new episodes can still miss on the same scan they're added in, due to a VideoLibrary commit-timing race -- deliberately not papered over with a blocking retry here, since that would only slow down the live scan without speeding up how fast files actually appear in Kodi; a missed NFO is caught on the episode's next scan, or immediately if "Automatically rebuild NFOs after every library scan" is enabled.) v2.13.1 - Fix: search_for_movie's filename pre-check (added in v2.13.0's own predecessor -- confirming whether a file already belongs to another item before creating a new one) crashed on every single call with "unsupported operand type(s) for -: int and str", silently degrading every movie search to title-only matching. Root cause: Kodi's find querystring carries year as a plain string; year_tolerant_match() does int arithmetic on it directly. New _parse_year() converts it before use, with a safe fallback to None on anything unparseable. v2.13.0 - New corner status indicator (the background service now shows a small "N item(s) processed so far" progress toast, the same widget the manual rebuild action already used for its own background phase) covering scraper activity that Kodi's own "Scanning library" indicator never did: that one only ever tracks Kodi's own directory-walk phase, not the tail of per-item find/getdetails/getartwork calls that follows it and can run for a long time afterward on a large library. Confirmed directly (2026-08-21): Kodi refuses actions like "Clean Library" the entire time that tail is still running, with nothing on screen explaining why -- this makes that activity visible instead of invisible. New lib/activity_tracker.py -- a small cross-process file-based signal, since every scraper action is Kodi's own short-lived, separate-process invocation with no other way for the one genuinely long-lived process (the background service) to know work is happening elsewhere. v2.12.0 - Two settings changes for anyone running this addon on more than one Kodi instance pointed at the same shared library (e.g. a primary box plus one or more Shields): (1) "Recreate local NFO file from Chronicle's data" is now OFF by default (was on). Kodi's own local-NFO-wins behaviour means only ONE instance needs to actually maintain the shared NFOs -- every other instance reading the same library just sees whatever that one instance already wrote, so leaving this off elsewhere avoids nothing but redundant work. Existing installs keep whatever they already had explicitly set; this only changes the out-of-the-box default for a fresh install. (2) New setting, "Include technical file info" (write_streamdetails, off by default, only enabled/visible when NFO writing itself is on): the <fileinfo><streamdetails> block added in v2.9.0 is now opt-in rather than automatic, since populating it needs a genuine extra JSON-RPC round-trip against Kodi's own library on top of the normal NFO write. Same reasoning as (1) -- only the instance responsible for the shared NFOs needs this turned on. v2.11.0 - BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: local movie-set (collection) artwork in Kodi's configured "Movie set information folder" is no longer fill-only -- Chronicle now overwrites whatever poster/fanart/banner/clearlogo/clearart/discart/thumb is already sitting there with its own current pick, every time a movie in that set gets scraped, the same way it already treats an individual movie's own local poster/fanart as its to overwrite (movie_art_sync.py). Previously, any file already present in a set's folder was left alone no matter what -- meant as a safeguard for hand-curated art, but it also meant a real correction made in Chronicle (a poster-language fix, a fallback pick when a collection had nothing of its own) could never actually reach this folder once ANY file already existed there, right or wrong. Confirmed directly (2026-08-21): two such fixes had already landed in Chronicle and simply never showed up locally for this reason. Whether a slot is pinned in Chronicle is still tracked and logged distinctly, but it no longer changes whether the write happens -- everything overwrites now, pinned or not. There is currently no way to exempt a specific hand-placed local file from being overwritten; if that turns out to matter, it needs its own follow-up. v2.10.0 - Two follow-ups to v2.9.0's local-NFO richness work, after reviewing the same class of problem in the two other places local data lives. (1) TV shows and episodes now get everything movies got in v2.9.0: a real tvshow.nfo and a per-episode NFO written from Chronicle's own data (title/plot/cast/genres/ratings/uniqueids/etc, plus a <fileinfo><streamdetails> block pulled from Kodi's own per-episode probe), local art file references, and -- via "Rebuild local NFOs from Chronicle", now extended to cover shows and episodes too, not just movies -- the same preserve-before-delete treatment: any data a previous tool's tvshow.nfo/episode NFO had that Chronicle doesn't is harvested and folded back in rather than lost. New lib/tvshow_location.py (the TV-side find_movie_location()), lib/tv_nfo_writer.py, and lib/nfo_common.py (XML-building blocks shared between the movie and TV writers, factored out rather than duplicated). Requires the current Chronicle server version -- /tv/episode-details now also returns the parent show's own title/year, which the addon needs to locate an episode's file on disk. (2) movieset-poster/fanart/etc. files (the movie-folder-embedded local convention "Rebuild local NFOs from Chronicle" already deleted) are no longer just discarded -- each one is copied into the dedicated Movie Set Information folder first if nothing is there already, so a previous tool's set art survives the rebuild the same way NFO data does. Also fixed: the background auto-rebuild service (Local Files -> "Automatically rebuild NFOs after every library scan", added in v2.7.0) had been silently crashing on every single run -- nfo_rebuild.run() returns a dict, not the 5-item tuple service.py's own caller still unpacked it as. v2.9.0 - Local NFOs are now much richer, and nothing they used to lose is lost anymore. (1) Kodi's own per-file technical info (video codec/resolution/HDR type, audio codec/language/channel count, subtitle track languages) is now written into a <fileinfo><streamdetails> block -- pulled live from Kodi's own VideoLibrary, since that's the only place this ever existed; Chronicle's server has no way to know a file's own technical makeup. (2) "Rebuild local NFOs from Chronicle" no longer just deletes whatever local NFO a previous tool (e.g. tinyMediaManager) left behind -- it's parsed first, stashed in this Kodi instance's own profile directory, then folded back in on the very next scrape: filling any gap Chronicle's own data has (a title/plot/cast/genres/ratings/etc. Chronicle never matched), AND contributed back into Chronicle itself via its own metadata-contribution endpoint, so it isn't lost a second time on the next rebuild. One-shot -- consumed and cleared the moment it's used, never a permanent shadow source. (3) The NFO's <art> block now also references every local image file already sitting in the movie's folder (extra fanart alternates, banner/clearart/clearlogo/discart, however they got there), not just Chronicle's own remote candidates -- by bare filename only, so it stays correct regardless of which Kodi instance (or which drive letter/mount convention that instance happens to use for the same share) ends up reading it. v2.8.0 - Collection (movie set) artwork, which until now was a single poster inherited from whichever member movie happened to carry belongsToCollection data. Chronicle now pulls every poster and backdrop TMDB holds for a collection (81 for Die Hard, 100 for Fast and Furious; 15,417 images across 598 collections in the reference library) and lets you choose which one is first class, exactly as you already could for a movie or show. Two things changed here to make that reach Kodi. (1) A movie set has no scraper hook at all -- Kodi never asks a scraper about one -- so its art can only arrive as files in the "Movie set information folder". That sync now writes every art type Kodi accepts (poster, fanart, banner, clearlogo, clearart, discart, thumb), not just poster and fanart; the rest existed in Chronicle and simply had no route here. (2) That sync has always been fill-only, so it never clobbers hand-curated files -- which also meant a poster you deliberately picked in Chronicle could never replace one already on disk. Fill-only now applies to automatically-resolved art only; a slot you explicitly pinned overwrites, because a pin is your choice and a more recent one than the file. Each overwrite is followed by a Textures.RemoveTexture call, since Kodi otherwise keeps serving its cached copy of the old image for up to a day even though the file underneath changed. v2.7.0 - The v2.5.0 "Rebuild local NFOs from Chronicle" action only ever fixed the library once, at the moment someone remembered to click it -- Chronicle's own data keeps changing afterward (re-matches, corrected collections, richer metadata) with no way for those changes to ever reach Kodi's local NFOs again, since Kodi never re-invokes this scraper for a file that already has ANY local NFO on disk, automatic or manual scan, no exceptions. New background service (new setting, Local Files -> "Automatically rebuild NFOs after every library scan", off by default) closes that loop: when on, every finished video library scan automatically re-runs the same delete-then-refresh rebuild the manual action performs, so Chronicle stays the actual source of truth for local NFO/set-art files going forward instead of only at one point in time. Deliberately opt-in and unconfirmed per run (a background service has no one to ask) -- the setting's own help text spells out the tradeoff (every other tool's local NFO data lost on every scan, full-library pass every time even for a one-file incremental scan). Runs on a background thread off Kodi's own event-handling thread so a long rebuild never stalls Kodi itself. v2.6.0 - Two more real bugs found and fixed during the v2.5.0 library-wide rebuild, both confirmed via live evidence, not guessed: (1) movie_art_sync's fast VideoLibrary-lookup path had no folder validation at all -- unlike the source-browsing fallback (already tightened in v2.5.0's predecessor fix), it blindly trusted whatever file Kodi's own title index returned for a search title. Caught live: "X" (2022) wrote its own correct art into the "X-Men (2000)" folder, because Kodi's stored title for that entry was ALSO still wrong (a self-reinforcing corruption -- Kodi's local-NFO-wins behaviour kept re-importing a stale NFO's wrong title on every touch, undoing a direct database correction each time, until the stale NFO itself was deleted). The fast path now verifies the returned file's own folder actually matches the searched title(+year) before trusting it, exactly like the slow path already did. (2) collection_sync now repairs stale set-art registrations, not just missing ones. Confirmed ~110 movie sets (out of ~177) had art registered against a share path ("Movie Collections" on an old share) that no longer exists at all following an earlier NAS reorganisation -- Kodi registers a set's art once and never re-checks it, so these showed permanently blank no matter how many times Chronicle correctly filled in art at the new location, since collection_sync only ever handled the MISSING case. Every sync_collection_art call now also verifies each of Kodi's own currently-registered local art paths still exists; a dead one gets repointed at the same-named file in the current set folder if one exists there, or cleared outright if not -- never left silently dangling. v2.5.0 - Adds the actual bulk mechanism the v2.4.0 NFO setting needed: "Rebuild local NFOs from Chronicle" (main addon menu, and an action button in Settings -> Local Files). The passive per-scrape NFO write can only ever help NEW movies -- it can't retroactively fix a library where local NFOs already exist, since Kodi never invokes this scraper for those at all. This action deletes every local .nfo and movieset-* file the whole movie library currently has, then forces a refresh per movie so Chronicle_Scraper gets invoked and repopulates them fresh -- i.e. exactly the manual delete-then-refresh procedure already run once by hand this session, now built into the addon itself. Shows a clear warning (irreversible, other tools' local data will be lost, can take a long time) and requires explicit confirmation before doing anything; a progress dialog allows cancelling mid-run. New shared lib/nfo_rebuild.py; movie_art_sync.py's timeout-guarded listdir helper is now public (listdir_with_timeout) so this reuses it instead of duplicating the same unresponsive-share protection. v2.4.0 - New setting (Local Files category), "Recreate local NFO file from Chronicle's data", defaulted ON. Root-caused (via the new v2.3.3 logging plus a live JSON-RPC VideoLibrary.RefreshMovie test against X-Men) why existing library items weren't picking up Chronicle's updates at all: Kodi checks for a movie's own local NFO before ever invoking this scraper, no exceptions, no settings toggle -- confirmed X-Men's ".nfo" was a real tinyMediaManager-authored file, meaning Chronicle_Scraper's find/getdetails never even ran for it on any subsequent scan, automatic or manual. Since tinyMediaManager only (re)writes an NFO when explicitly told to, a movie scraped once by it keeps that same NFO forever even as Chronicle's own data changes. Rather than fight Kodi's NFO-first behaviour, this addon now writes its own NFO every time it IS invoked (new addition, or NFO removed) using Chronicle's current data -- named to match the real video file's basename when known (e.g. "X-Men (2000).nfo"), which is confirmed to take precedence over a generic "movie.nfo" the same way a previous tool's NFO would. Refactored movie_art_sync.py's folder lookup into a shared find_movie_location() (now also surfaces the real video filename) so the new NFO writer and the existing art sync reuse a single lookup instead of each browsing the same video sources independently. v2.3.3 - Logging only, no behavior change: this addon's entire poster/collection-art path had almost no log visibility, making "why is this one movie/collection still showing a blank or stale poster" unanswerable from the log alone. Added: get_details/get_artwork now log Chronicle's full response summary (per-arttype candidate counts, whether a collection was present and whether it had a poster/backdrop) or an explicit warning when Chronicle returns nothing at all; find now logs the resolved item id/posterUrl or an explicit "no candidate" warning; apply_artwork logs exactly what gets pinned via setArt(); sync_movie_art logs the URL and destination path for every write attempt and explicitly logs when Chronicle has no candidate for a given art type; sync_collection_art now logs -- for the first time -- when a set's poster/fanart is skipped because a local file already exists (this module is fill-only and never overwrites, so a stale local file here can silently block every future update with zero prior trace) and logs the URL Chronicle currently has for that field so it can be compared against the stale file by hand. v2.3.2 - Fix (confirmed directly -- one worker thread stuck for 2+ minutes with kodi.log completely silent, while a live JSONRPC.Ping proved Kodi's own core was otherwise fully responsive): xbmcvfs.listdir() on an unresponsive SMB share doesn't raise or time out on its own, it just never returns. Since v2.3.1 expanded each multipath source into several real paths, one unresponsive share among them now means several separate chances to hang the whole scrape indefinitely instead of one. Every listdir() call in the source-browsing fallback now runs in a background thread with an 8s timeout; a share that doesn't answer in time is skipped (logged) rather than blocking the search forever. v2.3.1 - Fix (confirmed directly via kodi.log, not guessed): the v2.3.0 source-browsing fallback found the right folder name via xbmcvfs.listdir() on a multipath:// source (e.g. this user's bundled "Movies" source spanning several shares), then broke by re-appending that folder name onto the raw multipath:// string itself. multipath:// is a container Kodi's own listdir() browses transparently, not a real location -- appending a suffix to the whole bundle instead of to one of its real underlying paths produced a hard "XFILE::CDirectory::GetDirectory" error from Kodi's own core with no Python-catchable exception, so it silently looked like "no folder found" for every movie living under a multipath source whenever the VideoLibrary-lookup fast path missed (confirmed reproducible 3/3 times for The Union). Sources are now expanded into their real constituent paths up front, so nothing downstream ever builds a path against the bundle itself. v2.3.0 - movie_art_sync's cross-platform folder fallback (Files.GetSources + xbmcvfs.listdir, written in v2.2.1's development but never actually deployed) is now live. The VideoLibrary-only lookup from v2.2.1 could still miss movies that were already in the library at scan time if the title lookup didn't match cleanly (confirmed against The Union and X-Men still showing stale local posters after a rescan) -- this fallback browses the configured video sources directly by folder name instead of depending on VideoLibrary state at all. v2.2.1 - Confirmed directly (diagnostic build, not assumption) that Kodi's find/getdetails contract gives scrapers no path information on any channel -- querystring, cwd, or environment -- on any platform, since it's the same C++ core invocation everywhere. Also confirmed getartwork does not automatically follow getdetails, so movie_art_sync can't rely on it as a later retry. Added a short, early-exiting retry directly in movie_art_sync's VideoLibrary lookup to ride out the real, reproducible commit-timing race instead of silently giving up on the first miss. v2.2.0 - Added movie_art_sync: overwrites a movie's own local poster/fanart files (found via Kodi's own VideoLibrary, since the scraper contract never provides a file path) with Chronicle's current picks -- unlike collection sync, this deliberately overwrites, since the point is fixing stale leftover files from a previous scraper. Fixed collection_sync misreporting a failed image download as "folder not writable" -- only a genuine write failure implicates the folder now. v2.1.0 - Movie sets now sync into Kodi's own configured "Movie set information folder" (read live from Kodi's Settings API, never hardcoded) whenever a poster/fanart is missing there -- local folder art always wins over scraper-contributed art in Kodi, so this keeps it from silently going stale or blank when a set's local files are missing. Existing local art is never overwritten. Fixed: getdetails/getartwork now explicitly pin each item's own poster/fanart/etc via setArt() instead of only offering candidates, since Kodi doesn't reliably default-select the right one among several; the same fix applies to episode thumbnails. Added the getartwork action (movies and TV), which Kodi's own art-refresh flow calls separately from getdetails and which this addon previously silently ignored. v2.0.0 - Adds a full xbmc.metadata.scraper.tvshows extension point (show/season/episode), movie collections (Kodi movie sets, with set artwork), multi-source ratings, multi-candidate artwork, trailers, tagline/MPAA/country/studio/status, and cross-provider external IDs (IMDB/TVDB/TMDB/Trakt) -- all mined from data Chronicle already has across every configured metadata provider. Movies scraper rewritten on Kodi's modern InfoTagVideo API. v1.0.0 - Initial release: movie search/details backed by Chronicle's new /api/v1/scraper/movies endpoints. Connect to Chronicle via the same QR/PIN device-auth flow as Chronicle_Scrobbler.
